newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard stops ship with Asian immigrants.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard stops ship with Asian immigrants.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard has detained a ship carrying what are believed to be 69 undocumented Asian immigrants off the Mexican coast about 100 miles (160 km) south of here, officials said on Thursday.

The 150-foot (50 metre) vessel was intercepted Tuesday by a crew from the Coast Guard cutter Tybee, after it was spotted by aircraft, and was boarded Wednesday by four officers of the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service.

INS and Coast Guard officials, who identified the passengers as undocumented Asian migrants, were still on the scene 30 miles (48 km) off the Baja California coast in international waters Thursday morning. While the ship reportedly was flying a Mexican flag, its registry was not clear.
"We are providing humanitarian services -- food, water, that sort of thing, and the INS is still on board investigating," said Petty Officer Paul Rhynard, a Coast Guard spokesman.
The Coast Guard said 57 of the passengers are male and 12 are female; as many as two dozen may be children. No injuries or illnesses were reported on board.

In the past, ocean-going smugglers have dropped off their passengers in Mexico, where they began their trek north, mostly to Los Angeles, to seek asylum and work. For a while, U.S. State Department efforts to get Mexico to return undocumented immigrants trying to get into the United States were largely unsuccessful.

A similar incident off the coast of Mexico two years ago produced a short diplomatic standoff with the United States until the Mexican government agreed to escort a ship carrying 165 Chinese nationals into the port of Ensenada, where the passengers were unloaded and returned to China.
The U.S. State Department was in touch with the Mexican government, trying to work out a solution to the current situation.
